Russian draughts on an 8×8 board, dark squares only, 12 pieces per side. White moves first.
A man moves one step diagonally forward (toward the opponent).

Captures are mandatory when possible; if several capture sequences exist, you must choose one that removes the maximum number of opponent pieces.\n\nA man captures by jumping over an adjacent opponent to an empty square immediately beyond, in any diagonal direction. Multiple jumps in one turn are chained with the same piece. A man crowned on the last rank during a capture continues as a king.
A king moves any distance along a diagonal over empty squares. A king captures by jumping over exactly one opponent on that diagonal, landing on any empty square beyond it (long capture).

You win if the opponent has no pieces left or cannot move.\n\nComputer opponent: enable it in Settings, pick your color, and finish your capture chains when prompted. The current position is saved automatically and restored after you leave the app.
The computer uses a lookahead search (not perfect, but tricky).
White always moves first. If you play Black, the computer opens the game.
Higher levels search deeper moves (slower on weak devices).
Finish a game against the computer to see statistics.

Russian draughts on an 8×8 board, dark squares only, 12 pieces per side. White moves first.

A man moves one step diagonally forward (toward the opponent). Captures are mandatory when possible; if several capture sequences exist, you must choose one that removes the maximum number of opponent pieces.

A man captures by jumping over an adjacent opponent to an empty square immediately beyond, in any diagonal direction. Multiple jumps in one turn are chained with the same piece.

A king (crowned on the last rank) moves any distance along a diagonal over empty squares. A king captures by jumping over exactly one opponent on that diagonal, landing on any empty square beyond it (long capture).

You win if the opponent has no pieces left or cannot move.

Computer opponent: enable it in Settings, pick your color, and finish your capture chains when prompted. The current position is saved automatically and restored after you leave the app.
